title: SeeDNorm: Self-Rescaled Dynamic Normalization
claim: A drop-in replacement for the standard component consistently beats the baseline across language and vision tasks, with lower loss and faster convergence.
layout: 4 panels in a row; paired curves with double-arrow gap annotations
description: A single horizontal strip of four line plots, each comparing a blue baseline curve against a red curve for the proposed method. Panel 1 shows training loss against tokens (billions) for OLMoE-1.3B. Panel 2 shows downstream average accuracy against tokens for the same model. Panel 3 shows training loss against steps for a DiT-B/4 diffusion model, with a noisy trace. Panel 4 shows training loss against steps for ViT-B in MAE pre-training. The red curve sits below the blue one in the three loss plots and above it in the accuracy plot. Gray double-headed arrows mark the horizontal gap, labeled with a speedup such as x1.6, x1.9 or x1.3. A vertical arrow marks the final gap, such as 0.021, 4.6e-04 or 0.006. The eye goes first to the red-versus-blue separation.
caption: Comparisons between SeeDNorm and prior methods across diverse tasks in language modeling and vision. The first two figures respectively depict training loss curve comparisons and average downstream task1accuracy between the OLMoE-1.3B [22] baseline (using RMSNorm [41]) and the SeeDNorm-equipped model, following training on 500B tokens. The latter two figures show training loss comparisons between DyT-based [43] baseline models and SeeDNorm-based models in image generation and MAE [11] pre-training. All loss curves are smoothed with a 0.99 EMA.
abstract: Normalization layer constitutes an essential component in neural networks. In transformers, the predominantly used RMSNorm constrains vectors to a unit hypersphere, followed by dimension-wise rescaling through a learnable scaling coefficient $Î³$ to maintain the representational capacity of the model. However, RMSNorm discards the input norm information in forward pass and a static scaling factor $Î³$ may be insufficient to accommodate the wide variability of input data and distributional shifts, thereby limiting further performance improvements, particularly in zero-shot scenarios that large language models routinely encounter. To address this limitation, we propose SeeDNorm, which enhances the representational capability of the model by dynamically adjusting the scaling coefficient based on the current input, thereby preserving the input norm information and enabling data-dependent, self-rescaled dynamic normalization. During backpropagation, SeeDNorm retains the ability of RMSNorm to dynamically adjust gradient according to the input norm. We provide a detailed analysis of the training optimization for SeedNorm and proposed corresponding solutions to address potential instability issues that may arise when applying SeeDNorm. We validate the effectiveness of SeeDNorm across models of varying sizes in large language model pre-training as well as supervised and unsupervised computer vision tasks. By introducing a minimal number of parameters and with neglligible impact on model efficiency, SeeDNorm achieves consistently superior performance compared to previously commonly used normalization layers such as RMSNorm and LayerNorm, as well as element-wise activation alternatives to normalization layers like DyT.
